title: Cross Support Transfer Services—Monitored Data Service
organisation: Consultative Committee for Space Data Systems (CCSDS)
status_notes: The Document Control table (PDF p. 7) marks issue 2 (September 2022) as the current issue and 922.1-B-1 (April 2017) as superseded. Issue 2 is tied to issue 2 of the CSTS Specification Framework (CCSDS 921.1-B-2) and may only use that issue as a source of requirements (PDF pp. 12, 23).
summary:
The CCSDS Recommended Standard for the **Monitored Data Cross Support Transfer Service (MD-CSTS)**. CSTS is the family of cross support transfer services documented alongside the [SLE](../ccsds/sle/index.md) transfer services. Through MD-CSTS, a mission can watch the ground station that is supporting it. The mission can receive cyclic or on-change reports of monitored parameters, query current values, and receive notifications of events for everything in a service package: antennas, RF carriers, frame decoders, and the SLE and CSTS provider instances. The service delivers only current values, not history. It is built from procedures of the CSTS Specification Framework (CCSDS 921.1-B-2, not in the library) and uses the SANA Functional Resource registry to name parameters and events. The relevant wiki pages are [SLE service management](../ccsds/sle/service-management.md) and [SLE over TCP/IP and the SLE API](../ccsds/sle/isp1-and-api.md), since MD-CSTS PDUs are carried by ISP1.

Section 2 explains production and provision and the naming scheme. A Parameter Name combines a Parameter Identifier (an OID on the CCSDS registration tree) with a Functional Resource Name (type OID plus instance number), and Event Names are built the same way. Section 2 then gives a long operational scenario. Section 3 composes the service from four procedures: one Association Control; the prime On-Change-Option Cyclic Report (1..*); an optional Information Query (0..1); and Notification (0..*). Section 4 specifies the on-change extension to the framework Cyclic Report. Sections 5-7 refine Information Query and Notification and set the inherited configuration parameters. Sections 8-9 define the service-level functional resource items mdResponseTimeout, mdProdStat and mdProdStatChange. The annexes give the ICS proforma, the ASN.1 OIDs and PDUs, the production-process requirements, security and SANA considerations, and an informative example Functional Resource set (antenna, CCSDS 401 carriers, FCLTU and RAF providers).

key_points.text: MD-CSTS lets a mission receive cyclic reports on, and query current values of, the parameters of the cross support services provided by a Cross Support Complex (an Earth Space Link Terminal), and receive event notifications.
The standard does not define which parameters are reported or which events are notified, nor how they are measured.
The service delivers only current parameter values. It cannot deliver stored values from earlier times.
A service package may contain several MD-CSTS instances. Each instance can report all monitored parameters and events of the package, including RF links and SLE transfer service instances.
Implementations must use the SANA Functional Resource Registry as the normative source of Functional Resource Types, parameters and events. Annex F is only an example.

A Parameter Name combines a Parameter Identifier (a Published Identifier OID, for example ccsds-401-carrier-xmit-actual-carrier-freq) with a Functional Resource Name (Functional Resource Type OID plus a positive Functional Resource Instance Number assigned at scheduling).
The On-Change-Option Cyclic Report procedure lets the user choose a parameter list, a delivery cycle, and whether to report every value or only changed values. Several instances can run concurrently.
The service consists of Association Control (exactly 1), On-Change-Option Cyclic Report as prime procedure (1..*), Information Query (0..1) and Notification (0..*).
With the on-change option, a parameter whose value changes and changes back between two cycles is not reported.
Cyclic reporting of procedure configuration parameters is optional, because those parameters are static for the life of an MD service instance.

MD-CSTS supports the framework's response-timeout and production-status parameters (mdResponseTimeout, mdProdStat) and the production status change event (mdProdStatChange). It does not support the production configuration change event.
The Monitored Data Production Process must keep each monitored parameter's value until a new one is available. It delivers values as QualifiedParameter and events as [eventName: eventValue] pairs.

notes: PDF pages 1-2 are duplicate covers. The extracted text has 121 form-feed pages (registry: 120); the last one is empty. The running header reads 'Recommended Standard for CSTS Monitored Data Service'. The documentation-tree figure (1-1) and the scenario diagrams survive only as scattered labels. Oddities as printed: 3.2.13 sets the version number of the Notification procedure to '1', while Table 3-1 shows version 2 for it (PDF pp. 49-50); 3.3 refers to 'G3 of reference [1]' for the state machine; [G6] reads 'Recommendation for (Blue Book)'; and 'iInstance' appears in 2.2.2. The CSTS Specification Framework (921.1-B-2), the CSTS guidelines (921.2-M-1) and the SANA Functional Resource registry it depends on are not in the library. The informative SLE references are RAF B-4 and FCLTU B-4 (2016), while the library holds the later issue 5 of both (ccsds-911-1-911x1b5e1, ccsds-912-1-912x1b5e1). The library also holds the SCCS SM concept (ccsds-902-0-902x0g1), which named the Monitored Data service as forthcoming. No individual authors are named. The registry copy was taken from ccsds.org on 2026-11-12.
